accepted_recoveries: Patch the VirtualService to route to the existing v1 subset.
Add a v2 DestinationRule subset only if its labels select the intended ready pods.
forbidden_actions: Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.

incident.injected_fault: The checkout VirtualService routes to subset v2 while its DestinationRule defines only subset v1, whose labels match the ready checkout pods.
observable_signals: Checkout requests return HTTP 503 through the mesh ingress.
The ingress proxy reports no healthy upstream for checkout subset v2.
Direct requests to ready checkout pods succeed.
preconditions: The mesh control plane and ingress gateway are healthy.
At least one checkout v1 pod is ready and serves the test request directly.
No checkout v2 subset is defined before fault injection.
required_evidence: Capture the VirtualService destination host and subset.
Capture DestinationRule subset definitions and labels.
Capture ready checkout pod labels and a successful direct-pod probe.
Capture a failing ingress probe before recovery.
incident.title: VirtualService subset mismatch

constraints: Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.

hypotheses.cause: The checkout VirtualService routes traffic to subset v2, which is either undefined in DestinationRule or has no matching backend pods, whereas ready checkout pods are labeled with version=v1.
supports: Checkout pods in deployment checkout-gateway have label version=v1 and are in Ready state
Direct requests to checkout pods succeed while mesh ingress returns HTTP 503 with no healthy upstream for subset v2
Endpoints object contains active ready addresses (10.42.0.9:8080, 10.42.0.10:8080) for version=v1 pods

hypotheses.cause: Checkout backend pods or container processes are unready or failing application health checks.

Endpoints resource for checkout has two ready addresses

supports: Ingress proxy reports upstream connection failures returning HTTP 503

supports: Ingress proxy fails to resolve healthy upstream endpoints

payload.rationale: The checkout pods in deployment checkout-gateway are ready and labeled with version=v1. The VirtualService routes traffic to subset v2, which has no matching ready pods and is undefined in the DestinationRule, causing ingress 503 errors. Patching the VirtualService to route traffic to the existing v1 subset restores valid routing to healthy backend pods with minimal disruption.
payload.rollback_trigger: Mesh ingress HTTP 5xx error rate >= 0.001 or p95 latency >= 200ms persists after the VirtualService patch is applied.

success_criteria.description: Mesh ingress checkout requests return HTTP 200 with http_5xx_rate < 0.001 and p95_latency_ms < 200 across 3 consecutive evaluation windows.

VirtualService checkout was successfully patched to route traffic to the active v1 subset.

closure.summary: The checkout service incident caused by a VirtualService subset mismatch routing to an unbacked v2 subset was resolved by patching the VirtualService to target the existing v1 subset matching ready checkout-gateway pods. All SLO criteria have been verified and satisfied across 3 consecutive windows.
